questions.stem: How many chambers does the human heart have?
questions.explanation: The human heart has four chambers: two atria (upper chambers that receive blood) and two ventricles (lower chambers that pump blood out).

questions.stem: Which chamber pumps blood to the lungs?
questions.explanation: The right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood through the pulmonary artery to the lungs, where it picks up oxygen and releases carbon dioxide.

questions.stem: Why is the left ventricle wall thicker than the right ventricle wall?

options.text: It pumps blood at a slower rate
It needs to generate higher pressure to pump blood all around the body

questions.explanation: The left ventricle has a thicker muscular wall because it must generate enough pressure to pump blood through the aorta to all parts of the body, which is a much longer distance than to the lungs.

questions.stem: What is the function of the heart valves?

options.text: To prevent the backflow of blood and ensure it flows in one direction

questions.explanation: Heart valves (including the bicuspid, tricuspid, and semilunar valves) prevent blood from flowing backwards, ensuring it moves in one direction through the heart.

questions.stem: Which blood vessel carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart?
questions.explanation: The pulmonary vein is unique among veins because it carries oxygenated blood from the lungs back to the left atrium of the heart.

questions.stem: What separates the left and right sides of the heart?
questions.explanation: The septum is a thick wall of muscle that separates the left and right sides of the heart, preventing oxygenated and deoxygenated blood from mixing.

questions.stem: Which blood vessel is the largest artery in the body?
questions.explanation: The aorta is the largest artery in the body. It carries oxygenated blood from the left ventricle and branches into smaller arteries to supply the entire body.
